main_text.p: stus. Tandem concinnatum corpus omnibusq; suis partibus absolutum intelligente formatur anima, qua tunc est, & dicitur homo. Quoniam autem in procreatione hominis plurium animarum succefsio statuitur, idcirco quæruntnonnulli, an ipsæ animæ huiusmodi sint, ut quæ uegetans est nō decedat, sed à sentiente cōtineatur: Et hæc ab intelligente: an uel sentientis accefsu uegetans abeat, & intelligentis aduentu abolearur sentiens? Quòd si prior admittatur quæstio, in uno & eodem homine tres simul erunt animæ, uegetans, sentiens, & rationalis: quòd sane non solùm absurdum, sed & plane ridiculum est. Sic enim unus & idem homo erit plura, nempe & homo, & brutum, atq; planta. Si uero posterior uera sit, ter morietur fœtus, terq; renascetur. Primùm enim deleta uegetante interibit, & sentientis aduentu regenerabitur: qua rursum sublata, miser ille peribit: tertioque in postremæ animæ aduetu, qua homo est, morietur. Vt autem hæc diluatur ambigua, dicendum est aduentu intelligetis animæ, quæ secum omnem adducit animanti perfectionem, præcedentes adesse non ut formas essentiales, sed ut facultates, ac potestates,

page.notes: Long s rendered as s; Greek none. Catchword absent. Page is a faithful layout with the "D 4" signature at the foot. The scan is slightly faded; the word "states," at the line-end after the signature was taken as "states,", and the first-line fragment "stus." stays a fragment. Some words in the lower half were read with [?] where uncertain: "states," and the middle words of "uegetans" were read with care. Corrections needed in the first lines: "statuitur" and "decedat" are clear; "contineatur" is printed "cotineatur" and is transcribed as printed. Note that the transcription above is not final; check the printed lines "uero posterior uera sit" against the scan, as the scan reads "posterior ue ra fit".
